quizzes.question: A prompt asks you to 'design a notification system for 1M users.' What should you clarify BEFORE choosing Kafka or Redis?
options: Which Kubernetes ingress controller to install
Delivery channels, latency/durability expectations, expected peak burst, and acceptable duplicate rate
Whether to use JSON or YAML for config files
Which cloud vendor has cheaper managed Redis
quizzes.explanation: Requirements and constraints determine architecture; vendor tools like Kafka or Redis are implementation choices made after understanding workload shape.

quizzes.question: An API shows a 38ms average response time, yet support tickets report slowness. Which metric reveals the user pain most directly?
options: Mean latency sampled once per hour
p95 and p99 tail latency percentiles
quizzes.explanation: Averages hide skewed tails; p95/p99 expose the slowest 1–5% of requests affecting power users or multi-call pages.

quizzes.question: A service receives 43.2 million requests per day with a 5× peak burst multiplier. Roughly what is the Peak QPS?
quizzes.explanation: 43,200,000 / 86,400 seconds = 500 average QPS. Multiplying by 5× peak gives 2,500 Peak QPS.

quizzes.question: A gateway calls 20 independent backend services in parallel, each with a 1% chance (p99) of taking >500ms. Roughly how often does the user wait >500ms?
quizzes.explanation: Probability all 20 are fast is 0.99^20 ≈ 0.818, so 1 - 0.818 ≈ 18.2% of requests hit tail latency (tail amplification).

quizzes.question: You update a DNS A record from an old IP to a new IP with a previous TTL of 3600s. Why do some users still hit the old IP 20 minutes later?
options: TCP pins DNS records permanently in kernel space
Recursive resolvers and client caches retain the old record until the previous 3600s TTL expires
quizzes.explanation: DNS caches honor the TTL that was active when the record was cached; lower TTLs beforehand before cutovers.

quizzes.question: Why does HTTP/3 (QUIC over UDP) outperform HTTP/2 on lossy mobile networks?
options: QUIC multiplexes independent streams so losing one packet does not stall unrelated streams at the transport layer
quizzes.explanation: HTTP/2 suffers TCP head-of-line blocking when one TCP packet is lost; QUIC isolates packet loss per stream.

quizzes.question: You put a CDN in front of your API, yet origin bandwidth hardly drops. Which header is the most common culprit?
options: Cache-Control: private, no-store (or Vary: Cookie / Authorization)
quizzes.explanation: Private or cookie-varied responses bypass shared edge caches, forcing every request back to origin.

quizzes.question: One backend server becomes 5× slower due to GC pauses while others are fast. Which load-balancing algorithm adapts best without manual weights?
quizzes.explanation: Least-Connections notices the slow node's in-flight queue growing and automatically routes new requests to faster peers.

quizzes.question: A mobile client sends POST /charges, the payment succeeds, but the HTTP response drops on a tunnel disconnect. How do you make retrying safe?
options: Use HTTP GET instead of POST
Require a client-generated Idempotency-Key persisted atomically with the payment record
Increase TCP keepalive timeout to 10 minutes
quizzes.explanation: An Idempotency-Key lets the server recognize the retry and return the original 201 outcome instead of double-charging.

quizzes.question: You are building a financial double-entry ledger requiring strict multi-row balance invariants. Which data model fits best?
options: Relational SQL database with ACID transactions
quizzes.explanation: Relational databases enforce ACID multi-row atomicity, foreign-key constraints, and strict serializability for monetary invariants.

quizzes.question: Why are LSM-Tree storage engines (e.g., RocksDB) often chosen over B+Trees for write-heavy ingestion workloads?
options: LSM-Trees store all data in RAM with no disk persistence
LSM-Trees convert random mutations into sequential WAL + MemTable appends and periodic SSTable compaction
quizzes.explanation: Sequential writes maximize disk throughput; Bloom filters mitigate read amplification across SSTables.

quizzes.question: A table has a composite B-Tree index on (org_id, created_at). Which query CANNOT efficiently use this index alone?
options: WHERE org_id = 42 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20
quizzes.explanation: Because of the leftmost-prefix rule, filtering only on the second column (created_at) cannot seek efficiently in (org_id, created_at).

quizzes.question: Two transactions concurrently check that >= 2 doctors are on call, then each updates a DIFFERENT doctor's row to off-duty, leaving 0 on call. Which isolation level blocks this anomaly?
quizzes.explanation: Write skew happens across disjoint rows under Snapshot Isolation; Serializable (or explicit SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) prevents it.

quizzes.question: How should a system handle 2 GB video uploads without exhausting API server memory and worker threads?
options: Base64-encode the 2 GB file inside a JSON POST body
Issue short-lived presigned URLs so clients upload multipart chunks directly to object storage
Store chunks as BLOB columns in the primary PostgreSQL table
Stream uploads through the auth service
quizzes.explanation: Presigned multipart URLs keep heavy binary payload traffic off application servers while retaining auth control.

quizzes.question: What is the biggest hazard of Write-Behind (Write-Back) caching compared to Cache-Aside?
options: A cache node crash before asynchronous flush loses acknowledged writes
quizzes.explanation: Write-Behind ACKs writes in memory before persisting to durable storage, risking data loss on sudden cache failure.

quizzes.question: A nightly batch backup reads millions of cold records once through an LRU cache, wiping out hot user profiles. What is this called, and how does TinyLFU help?
options: Cache stampede; solved by increasing TTL
Cache pollution (scan resistance failure); TinyLFU uses frequency sketches to reject one-hit cold keys
quizzes.explanation: Pure LRU promotes one-time scan keys; frequency-aware admission (Window-TinyLFU) protects hot items.

quizzes.question: A hot key expires and 1,000 concurrent requests miss Redis at once, crashing the database. Which combination solves both the burst and synchronized expiry?
quizzes.explanation: Singleflight ensures only 1 in-flight DB fetch per key; TTL jitter spreads expiration times so keys do not expire together.

quizzes.question: You autoscale from 20 to 200 microservice pods, each opening 25 DB connections, and PostgreSQL fails with 'too many clients'. What fixes this?
options: Place a connection pooler (e.g., PgBouncer transaction pooling) in front of PostgreSQL and bound per-pod pool sizes
Disable TLS between app and DB
quizzes.explanation: 200 × 25 = 5,000 connections overwhelms PostgreSQL process memory/locks; transaction pooling multiplexes thousands of app sockets onto bounded DB connections.

quizzes.question: A user edits their profile (writes to Leader) and immediately reloads the page (reads from an async Replica), seeing old data. Which guarantee was violated?
quizzes.explanation: Read-your-writes can be restored by routing the user's own reads to the leader briefly after a write or checking replication LSN offsets.

quizzes.question: Why do production consistent-hashing rings assign 50–200 virtual nodes per physical shard instead of just 1 position per shard?
options: To keep key distribution balanced and spread a failed shard's load evenly across all remaining shards
To turn hash partitioning into range queries
To remove the need for replication
quizzes.explanation: With 1 token per node, key distribution skews heavily and one neighbor absorbs 100% of a failed node's traffic; vnodes smooth variance.

quizzes.question: A single celebrity account receives 40% of all writes in a hash-sharded table. How do you break the single-shard bottleneck?
options: Increase the shard key string length
Append a bounded random salt suffix (e.g., user_id#0..9) for writes and fan out reads across those 10 sub-keys
quizzes.explanation: Key salting spreads hot writes across K shards at the trade-off of reading/aggregating K sub-keys on read.

quizzes.question: Why does UUIDv7 (or Snowflake ID) outperform random UUIDv4 as a clustered B-Tree primary key on large relational tables?
options: Time-ordered IDs append sequentially at the right edge of the B-Tree, avoiding random page splits and buffer-pool thrashing
quizzes.explanation: Random UUIDv4 keys insert across random disk pages, causing 50%-full fragmented pages and heavy random I/O.

quizzes.question: A Kafka topic has 4 partitions and a consumer group scales up to 6 identical consumer instances. How many instances stay idle?
options: 2 — at most 1 consumer per group can read a partition simultaneously
quizzes.explanation: In Kafka consumer groups, partition count caps parallel consumers within a single group; 6 consumers on 4 partitions leaves 2 idle.

quizzes.question: A malformed 'poison pill' event crashes a worker repeatedly under at-least-once delivery, blocking healthy messages behind it. What fixes this?
options: Bounded retries with exponential backoff + Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) quarantine + alerting
quizzes.explanation: Routing unprocessable messages to a DLQ after N retries preserves queue throughput while keeping failed events inspectable.

quizzes.question: An Order service commits to PostgreSQL and then tries to publish an OrderCreated event to Kafka, but crashes right between the two calls. Which pattern fixes this dual-write bug?
options: Transactional Outbox (write order + outbox row in one DB transaction, relay via CDC/poller)
quizzes.explanation: Writing business state and outbox event atomically inside one local ACID transaction guarantees at-least-once event publishing.

quizzes.question: Why do teams keep a dedicated inverted index (e.g., OpenSearch/Elasticsearch) synced asynchronously via CDC instead of running LIKE '%term%' on a 500M-row PostgreSQL table?
options: Leading-wildcard LIKE scans cannot use standard B-Tree prefixes and trigger full scans, whereas inverted indexes map tokens directly to doc lists with BM25 scoring
PostgreSQL cannot store strings longer than 255 bytes
B-Trees do not support equality lookups
quizzes.explanation: Inverted indexes pre-tokenize text into term → posting-list lookups with relevance ranking (BM25).

quizzes.question: In event-time stream processing, what is a watermark?
options: A PNG logo placed on video frames
A heuristic timestamp threshold declaring that no earlier events are expected for a window, trading completeness vs latency
quizzes.explanation: Watermarks bound how long a streaming window waits for delayed/out-of-order mobile events before emitting an aggregate.

quizzes.question: 10,000 clients time out simultaneously and use deterministic exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s) WITHOUT jitter. What happens?
options: All 10,000 clients retry in synchronized thundering waves, repeatedly knocking the recovering server back down
quizzes.explanation: Full jitter randomizes delay within [0, cap] to desynchronize client retries and let dependencies recover.

quizzes.question: Worker A acquires a Redis lock, pauses 20s for Stop-The-World GC past lease TTL, and wakes up thinking it still holds the lock while Worker B is active. What prevents Worker A from corrupting storage?
options: Monotonic fencing tokens verified by the storage server on every write
quizzes.explanation: The storage layer rejects writes carrying a fencing token older than the highest token it has already observed.

quizzes.question: A Dynamo-style store has N=5 replicas and W=2. What minimum Read Quorum (R) guarantees overlapping at least one latest-written replica (ignoring sloppy quorums)?
quizzes.explanation: R + W > N requires R + 2 > 5, so R >= 4 guarantees at least 1 overlapping replica.

quizzes.question: A 5-node Raft cluster splits into a 3-node side and a 2-node side during a network partition. What happens?
options: Both sides elect leaders and accept writes
The 3-node majority elects/keeps a leader and commits writes; the 2-node minority cannot reach quorum (3) and halts writes
quizzes.explanation: Majority quorum (floor(5/2)+1 = 3) guarantees at most one partition side can elect a leader, preventing split-brain.

quizzes.question: Why should you NOT route high-throughput user business payloads through etcd or ZooKeeper?
options: They are consensus-backed coordination stores optimized for small metadata, leases, and config—not high-QPS bulk data
They cannot persist data to disk
quizzes.explanation: Consensus replication across a quorum adds RTT coordination cost; keep etcd/ZK on the control plane.

quizzes.question: A checkout service is at 140% CPU capacity with an unbounded FIFO request queue, so requests wait 15 seconds and time out anyway. What stabilizes core checkout goodput?
options: Increase the FIFO queue limit to 1 million
Bound queues + LIFO/priority load shedding rejecting low-priority calls fast with 503 + Retry-After
quizzes.explanation: Unbounded FIFO queues create cascading timeout waste; shedding excess or lower-priority work early preserves p99 for admitted requests.

quizzes.question: Why is putting raw `user_id` as a Prometheus metric label usually an anti-pattern?
options: High-cardinality labels explode time-series memory and index size; high-cardinality IDs belong in structured logs and trace spans
quizzes.explanation: Metrics need bounded cardinality (route, status, region); use structured logs and OpenTelemetry trace spans for per-user/request debugging.

quizzes.question: A Fixed-Window rate limiter enforces 100 req/min, yet a client sends 200 requests between 12:00:55 and 12:01:05. Why?
options: Boundary burst: 100 requests fit at the end of minute 0 and 100 at the start of minute 1
quizzes.explanation: Fixed windows allow up to 2× limit across minute edges; Sliding Window Counter or Token Bucket avoids sharp boundary spikes.

quizzes.question: What distinguishes a Canary deployment from a Blue/Green deployment?
options: Canary shifts a small traffic slice (e.g., 1%→10%) validated by SLO metrics before full rollout; Blue/Green switches 100% of traffic between two full environments
quizzes.explanation: Canary limits blast radius to a small percentage of live requests gated by error/latency SLOs.

quizzes.question: A disaster recovery SLA specifies RPO <= 5 seconds and RTO <= 2 minutes. What do these mean?
options: Max 5s of recent committed data loss on failover; max 2m of downtime to restore service
5 backups per year; 2 TB max database
quizzes.explanation: RPO bounds data loss across replication lag/backups; RTO bounds total recovery duration.

quizzes.question: What belongs in an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) that regular code comments miss?
options: Context/constraints, alternatives considered, explicit trade-offs accepted, and validation signals that would trigger revisiting the choice
quizzes.explanation: ADRs preserve *why* a consequential architectural trade-off was chosen over rejected alternatives.

quizzes.question: Why do production LLM gateways meter rate limits by tokens-per-minute (TPM) and stream responses over SSE instead of standard RPM + buffered JSON?
options: One prompt with 32K tokens consumes vastly more GPU KV-cache and compute than a 50-token prompt, and SSE streams tokens immediately to minimize perceived wait
quizzes.explanation: Token volume dictates GPU memory/compute saturation, while SSE delivers low Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) UX.

quizzes.question: When migrating a busy monolith to an extracted service using the Strangler Fig pattern, what is the safest sequence?
options: Shut down the monolith for a weekend rewrite
Put an edge router/proxy in front, verify the new service via shadow reads/CDC sync, shift traffic incrementally (1%→100%), then retire old routes
Share the same in-memory heap across networks
quizzes.explanation: Strangler Fig reduces cutover risk through progressive routing, data parity checks, and instant rollback.

flashcards.front: Seconds in a day (for QPS math)
flashcards.back: 86,400 seconds (~10^5 for rough mental bounds; exact 86,400 for clean estimates).
L = λ × W (Average concurrent items in system = Arrival rate × Average time spent in system).
If a page calls N independent services each with p99 slowness, P(any slow) = 1 - (0.99)^N.
flashcards.hook: At N=30 calls, ~26% of user loads hit tail latency.

flashcards.back: Multiple global edge PoPs announce the same IP via BGP; routers naturally direct users to the topologically closest healthy PoP.
flashcards.hook: Used by DNS roots and CDNs like Cloudflare.

flashcards.back: In HTTP/2 over TCP, 1 lost packet stalls all multiplexed streams. QUIC (HTTP/3) runs over UDP so streams recover independently.
flashcards.hook: Stream isolation = faster mobile tail latency.

flashcards.back: s-maxage overrides max-age specifically for shared caches (CDNs/proxies), letting edge cache longer than browsers.
Client-generated unique UUID per logical action stored atomically by the server so network retries return the original result without duplicating side effects.
flashcards.hook: Essential for POST /payments and order creation.

flashcards.back: B+Tree = fast predictable point/range reads, random page writes. LSM-Tree = sequential append-only writes (WAL+MemTable), background compaction & Bloom filters.
flashcards.hook: Read-heavy SQL → B+Tree; Write-heavy log/KV → LSM.

flashcards.back: Answers 'Definitely NOT in SSTable' (0% false negatives) or 'Possibly in SSTable' (small tunable false positive rate).
flashcards.hook: Saves unnecessary disk seeks on missing keys.

flashcards.back: An index containing all columns required by the query (SELECT + WHERE), avoiding table heap lookups completely.
Two concurrent transactions read overlapping sets and update disjoint rows, breaking a cross-row invariant under Snapshot Isolation.
flashcards.hook: Prevented by Serializable (SSI) or SELECT FOR UPDATE.

flashcards.back: API authorizes short-lived signed URLs; client uploads chunks directly to object storage (S3/R2), bypassing API server bandwidth.
flashcards.hook: Keep DB for metadata, Object Store for blobs.

flashcards.back: Write-Through updates cache + DB synchronously (safe, slower write). Write-Behind updates cache and flushes DB async (ultra-fast, crash risk).
flashcards.hook: Never use Write-Behind for non-recoverable ledger writes.

flashcards.front: Cache Stampede vs Cache Penetration vs Cache Avalanche
flashcards.back: Stampede = 1 hot key expires under concurrency (fix: Singleflight). Penetration = misses for nonexistent keys hit DB (fix: Bloom filter/null cache). Avalanche = mass synchronized expiry (fix: TTL jitter).
Relational DBs allocate ~5–10MB RAM + lock slots per backend connection; pooling multiplexes 1000s of stateless pod requests onto ~50–100 DB connections.
Guaranteeing a user immediately sees their own committed mutation by routing their short-window reads to the leader or tracking replica LSN.
flashcards.hook: Prevents 'I saved my post and it vanished!' bugs.

flashcards.back: Adding or removing 1 node out of N remaps only ~1/N of keys (vs ~N/(N+1) with modulo hash % N).
flashcards.hook: Virtual nodes prevent skewed shard hotspots.

flashcards.back: 1) Expand (add new col/table), 2) Dual-write + Backfill, 3) Shadow verify reads, 4) Switch reads & Contract old column.
1 unused sign bit + 41 bits ms timestamp (~69 yrs) + 10 bits worker/datacenter ID (1024 nodes) + 12 bits sequence (4096 IDs/ms/node).

flashcards.front: Work Queue vs Partitioned Append-Only Log
flashcards.back: Queue deletes messages after worker ACK. Log retains events by offset so multiple independent consumer groups can replay history.
Insert domain row + outbox event row in one local ACID transaction; Debezium/relay reads WAL/outbox to publish reliably without 2PC.
Break cross-service transaction into local steps; if step K fails, execute compensating undo actions for steps K-1 down to 1.
Scores documents higher for rare matching query terms (IDF) and term frequency with diminishing returns (TF), normalized by document length.
sleep = random(0, min(cap, base × 2^attempt)) — spreads concurrent retry storms across the whole interval.
Closed (normal) → Open (fail fast after error threshold) → Half-Open (let probe request test recovery).
NTP steps forward or backward on clock sync; use monotonic clocks for elapsed durations and logical/Lamport clocks or fencing tokens for ordering.
R + W > N ensures read quorum overlaps with write quorum on >= 1 node holding the latest value.
flashcards.hook: Does NOT automatically mean linearizability without read-repair/coordination.

flashcards.back: If Partition (P): choose Availability (A) or Consistency (C); Else (E) normal operation: choose Latency (L) or Consistency (C).
flashcards.hook: Explains why DynamoDB/Cassandra trade consistency for low latency even without partitions.

flashcards.back: 1 - SLO (e.g., 99.9% availability SLO = 0.1% or ~43.2 min/month allowable downtime). When exhausted, freeze risky releases and focus on reliability.
flashcards.hook: Aligns dev velocity and SRE stability.

flashcards.back: JWT allows stateless signature verification but is hard to revoke immediately before exp. Opaque tokens hit Redis/DB for instant revocation.
flashcards.hook: Short-lived JWT (5–15m) + revocable refresh token balances both.

flashcards.back: Embed incoming query into vector store; if cosine similarity exceeds high threshold (e.g., >0.95), return cached completion in <40ms at $0 GPU cost.

interviewPrompts.title: Design a URL Shortener (TinyURL / bit.ly)
interviewPrompts.prompt: Design a service that shortens long URLs into 7-character codes and redirects 100M DAU at 100:1 read/write ratio.
bottlenecks: Collision-safe short code generation (Base62 counter/KGS vs random + retry)
Hot viral link cache stampede defense (CDN + Redis + singleflight)
Async click analytics decoupled via queue

interviewPrompts.title: Design a Distributed API Rate Limiter
interviewPrompts.prompt: Protect microservices at 500K RPS with configurable per-user and per-IP rate limits across multiple API gateway instances.
clarifications: Hard global exactness vs fast local approximate quota?
Fail-open vs fail-closed if Redis is unreachable?
bottlenecks: Atomic read-check-decrement in Redis using Lua scripts
Sliding Window Counter / Token Bucket to stop boundary 2× bursts
Sub-millisecond hot-path latency budget

interviewPrompts.title: Design a Multi-Channel Notification Service
interviewPrompts.prompt: Send 50M push, email, and SMS alerts daily with priority lanes (OTP < 2s vs marketing batch) and user opt-out preferences.
clarifications: Per-channel vendor rate limits and failover providers?
bottlenecks: Separate priority queues so marketing spikes never delay OTP codes
Transactional Outbox + worker idempotency keys to avoid duplicate SMS
Circuit breakers + DLQ around flaky third-party SMS/SMTP providers

interviewPrompts.title: Design a Social News Feed / Home Timeline
interviewPrompts.prompt: Support 50M DAU posting text/media and loading personalized feeds under 200ms p95, including celebrity accounts with 20M followers.
bottlenecks: Hybrid fan-out: push-on-write for regular users, pull-on-read merge for celebrities
Cursor-based pagination (avoiding OFFSET drift)
Pre-computed feed caches + object storage CDN for images

interviewPrompts.title: Design Real-Time Chat & Online Presence
interviewPrompts.prompt: Design 1:1 and group chat (up to 500 members) with read receipts, offline message sync, and accurate online/last-seen presence.
clarifications: Message ordering guarantee (server-assigned sequence vs Snowflake)?
bottlenecks: Stateful WebSocket gateway fleet + session routing registry
Presence heartbeat storms mitigated via batching/client TTLs
Time-series / LSM partition design (`channel_id, message_id`)

interviewPrompts.title: Design a Payment Processing & Double-Entry Ledger
interviewPrompts.prompt: Process 5,000 TPS of marketplace checkouts and payouts with zero lost or double-counted money across retries and PSP outages.
clarifications: Synchronous authorization vs async settlement reconciliation?
bottlenecks: Double-entry append-only ledger (`debit + credit = 0`) under Serializable/locking
End-to-end Idempotency-Keys across client → API → PSP
Async reconciliation jobs catching drifted webhook states

interviewPrompts.title: Design Flash-Sale Ticket Booking & Seat Reservation
interviewPrompts.prompt: Handle 100K concurrent buyers racing for 20,000 concert seats with 10-minute checkout holds and zero double-booked seats.
clarifications: Specific seat map selection vs general admission?
Bot/scalper rate limiting & virtual waiting room?
bottlenecks: Virtual waiting room shedding burst traffic before touching DB
Optimistic version check / Redis TTL seat lock + DB unique constraint
Lease expiration sweeper releasing abandoned holds reliably

interviewPrompts.title: Design a Multi-Tenant Enterprise RAG & LLM Platform
interviewPrompts.prompt: Serve 10,000 organizations querying private documents via RAG + streaming LLM completions with strict tenant isolation and token quotas.
clarifications: Document ACL enforcement (ReBAC) inside vector retrieval?
bottlenecks: Pre-filtering or metadata-partitioned vector + BM25 hybrid retrieval respecting ACLs
Semantic caching + continuous GPU batching + SSE token streaming
Per-tenant token-bucket TPM quotas preventing noisy-neighbor GPU starvation
